mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces the cost of capital for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to recession fears.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in monthly payroll growth (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signal robust labor market conditions, which correlate with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as corporate earnings growth is sustained.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (defined by GDP growth above 3.0% annualized and CPI inflation exceeding 3.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns due to accelerating monetary tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3.0% annualized and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to accelerate rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200.0 units signals strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, which typically produces positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to immediate market reaction to positive economic data.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly retail sales increase (RSAFS) above 470,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns as earnings growth sustains equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS > 470000.
